why: Every question the game can ask, and nothing only the pipeline reads. Only the status:'live' records reach this file — every other record is held back until its gates pass. Generated, never hand-edited: fix the record and re-run tools/build-questions.py.

questions.questionText: Which planet is third from the Sun?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet is third from the Sun?
questions.correctVoiceText: Well done! Earth is number three from the Sun. Earth is the third planet from the Sun, and the biggest of the four rocky planets.
questions.teachingFactText: Earth is the third planet from the Sun, and the biggest of the four rocky planets.

questions.questionText: How many natural moons does Earth have?
questions.questionVoiceText: How many natural moons does Earth have?
questions.correctVoiceText: You got it! Earth has one natural moon. Earth has one natural moon — the Moon we see shining in our night sky.
questions.teachingFactText: Earth has one natural moon — the Moon we see shining in our night sky.

questions.questionText: Do we ever see the far side of the Moon from Earth?
questions.questionVoiceText: Do we ever see the far side of the Moon from Earth?
questions.correctAnswer: No — the Moon keeps its same face towards us
choices: No — the Moon keeps its same face towards us
questions.correctVoiceText: That's right! We only ever see one side of the Moon. The Moon keeps the same face turned towards Earth, so we only ever see one side of it.
questions.teachingFactText: The Moon keeps the same face turned towards Earth, so we only ever see one side of it.

questions.questionText: Earth has one natural moon. What is it called?
questions.questionVoiceText: Earth has one natural moon. What is it called?
questions.correctVoiceText: Yes! A moon is a world that travels around a planet. Earth has one natural moon, and we call it the Moon.
questions.teachingFactText: Earth has one natural moon, and we call it the Moon.

questions.questionText: Which of the four rocky planets is the biggest?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which of the four rocky planets is the biggest?
questions.correctVoiceText: Spot on! The other rocky planets are Mercury, Venus and Mars. Earth is the biggest of the four rocky planets.
questions.teachingFactText: Earth is the biggest of the four rocky planets.

questions.questionText: Which gas in the air on Earth do we need to breathe?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which gas in the air on Earth do we need to breathe?
questions.correctVoiceText: Well done! Most of the air is a gas called nitrogen. The air on Earth has the oxygen we need to breathe.
questions.teachingFactText: The air on Earth has the oxygen we need to breathe.

questions.questionText: Why do we get seasons on Earth?
questions.questionVoiceText: Why do we get seasons on Earth?
choices: Earth's air is thinner in winter
The Moon pulls on the tides
questions.correctVoiceText: Brilliant! Earth's tilt stays the same all year round. Earth is tilted on its axis, and that tilt gives us our seasons.
questions.teachingFactText: Earth is tilted on its axis, and that tilt gives us our seasons.

questions.questionText: Why does the Moon's bright shape change through the month?
questions.questionVoiceText: Why does the Moon's bright shape change through the month?
questions.correctAnswer: We see a different part of its sunlit side
choices: We see a different part of its sunlit side
The Moon changes its own shape
questions.correctVoiceText: That's it! The Sun always shines on one half of the Moon. As the Moon goes round Earth, one part is in sunlight, then another.
questions.teachingFactText: As the Moon goes round Earth, one part is in sunlight, then another.

questions.questionText: Which planet is the largest in our solar system?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet is the largest in our solar system?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's it! Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system. It is the biggest of all eight planets.
questions.teachingFactText: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.

questions.questionText: What kind of planet is Jupiter?
questions.questionVoiceText: What kind of planet is Jupiter?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's it! Some planets are made of gas instead of rock. Jupiter is a gas giant, not a rocky world.
questions.teachingFactText: Jupiter is a gas giant, not a rocky world.

questions.questionText: Which planet is the fifth one out from the Sun?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet is the fifth one out from the Sun?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's right! Jupiter is much further out from the Sun than Earth is. Jupiter is the fifth planet out from the Sun.
questions.teachingFactText: Jupiter is the fifth planet out from the Sun.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the biggest moon in the whole solar system?
questions.questionVoiceText: What is the name of the biggest moon in the whole solar system?
questions.correctVoiceText: You got it! Ganymede is even bigger than the planet Mercury. The biggest moon in the whole solar system is Jupiter's Ganymede.
questions.teachingFactText: The biggest moon in the whole solar system is Jupiter's Ganymede.

questions.questionText: Which planet spins round faster than any other, giving it the shortest day?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet spins round faster than any other, giving it the shortest day?
questions.correctVoiceText: Yes! A full turn of a planet's spin is its day. Jupiter spins so fast that it has the shortest day of any planet.
questions.teachingFactText: Jupiter spins so fast that it has the shortest day of any planet.

questions.questionText: Which of Jupiter's moons has more volcanic activity than any other world?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which of Jupiter's moons has more volcanic activity than any other world?
questions.correctVoiceText: Spot on! Jupiter's pull squeezes and stretches Io, and that makes its inside hot enough to melt rock. Jupiter's moon Io has more volcanic activity than any other world.
questions.teachingFactText: Jupiter's moon Io has more volcanic activity than any other world.

questions.questionText: How many moons does Mars have?
questions.questionVoiceText: How many moons does Mars have?
questions.correctVoiceText: Brilliant! Mars has two moons. Mars has two small moons, called Phobos and Deimos.
questions.teachingFactText: Mars has two small moons, called Phobos and Deimos.

questions.questionText: What is Mars's larger moon called?
questions.questionVoiceText: What is Mars's larger moon called?
questions.correctVoiceText: Yes! Phobos is Mars's larger moon. Phobos is a little larger than Deimos, so it is the larger of Mars's two moons.
questions.teachingFactText: Phobos is a little larger than Deimos, so it is the larger of Mars's two moons.

questions.questionText: Why does Mars look red?
questions.questionVoiceText: Why does Mars look red?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's right! Mars is a cold, dusty desert. Rusty iron in the soil gives Mars its red colour.
questions.teachingFactText: Rusty iron in the soil gives Mars its red colour.

questions.questionText: Mars is a dusty world, but it has white caps at its poles. What are they made of?
questions.questionVoiceText: Mars is a dusty world, but it has white caps at its poles. What are they made of?
questions.correctVoiceText: You got it! Ice is water that has frozen solid. Mars has frozen ice caps at its north and south poles.
questions.teachingFactText: Mars has frozen ice caps at its north and south poles.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the biggest volcano in the whole solar system?
questions.questionVoiceText: What is the name of the biggest volcano in the whole solar system?
questions.correctVoiceText: Yes! A volcano is a mountain that can puff out hot rock. The biggest volcano in the whole solar system stands on Mars.
questions.teachingFactText: The biggest volcano in the whole solar system stands on Mars.

questions.questionText: Which of Mars's two moons travels farther out from Mars?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which of Mars's two moons travels farther out from Mars?
questions.correctVoiceText: Spot on! A moon that travels farther out takes longer to go all the way round. Deimos is the moon that travels farther from Mars.
questions.teachingFactText: Deimos is the moon that travels farther from Mars.

questions.questionText: Who was Mars named after?
questions.questionVoiceText: Who was Mars named after?
choices: The Roman god of the sea
The Greek god of the sea
questions.correctVoiceText: Well done! The ancient Romans named lots of planets after their gods. The Romans gave Mars its name after their god of war.
questions.teachingFactText: The Romans gave Mars its name after their god of war.

questions.questionText: How many times does Phobos go right around Mars in one day on Mars?
questions.questionVoiceText: How many times does Phobos go right around Mars in one day on Mars?
questions.correctVoiceText: Brilliant! Phobos is a small, fast-moving moon of Mars. Phobos whizzes around Mars three times in each Mars day.
questions.teachingFactText: Phobos whizzes around Mars three times in each Mars day.

questions.questionText: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.correctVoiceText: Yes! Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun. As well as being nearest to the Sun, Mercury is the smallest of all eight planets.
questions.teachingFactText: As well as being nearest to the Sun, Mercury is the smallest of all eight planets.

questions.questionText: The hottest planet is not the closest one to the Sun. Which planet is the hottest?
questions.questionVoiceText: The hottest planet is not the closest one to the Sun. Which planet is the hottest?
questions.correctVoiceText: Spot on! Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system. Venus is hotter than every other planet — even Mercury, which is nearer to the Sun.
questions.teachingFactText: Venus is hotter than every other planet — even Mercury, which is nearer to the Sun.

questions.questionText: Which planet is the second one out from the Sun?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet is the second one out from the Sun?
questions.correctVoiceText: Brilliant! Venus is the planet next door to Earth. Venus is the second planet out from the Sun.
questions.teachingFactText: Venus is the second planet out from the Sun.

questions.questionText: Which planet is the smallest of the eight?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet is the smallest of the eight?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's it! Mercury is a small, rocky planet. Mercury is the smallest of all eight planets.
questions.teachingFactText: Mercury is the smallest of all eight planets.

questions.questionText: Almost all of the thick air around Venus is one gas. Which gas?
questions.questionVoiceText: Almost all of the thick air around Venus is one gas. Which gas?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's right! Venus is wrapped in a blanket of air. Almost all of Venus's thick air is carbon dioxide.
questions.teachingFactText: Almost all of Venus's thick air is carbon dioxide.

questions.questionText: If you stood on Venus, which way would the Sun rise?
questions.questionVoiceText: If you stood on Venus, which way would the Sun rise?
questions.correctVoiceText: You got it! Venus turns the opposite way from most planets. On Venus the Sun would rise in the west.
questions.teachingFactText: On Venus the Sun would rise in the west.

questions.questionText: Which planet is known for its rings?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet is known for its rings?
questions.correctVoiceText: Spot on! Saturn is the planet known for its rings. Other planets have rings too, but none are as spectacular or as complex as Saturn's.
questions.teachingFactText: Other planets have rings too, but none are as spectacular or as complex as Saturn's.

questions.questionText: Which planet is the second biggest in the solar system?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet is the second biggest in the solar system?
questions.correctVoiceText: Well done! Saturn is much bigger than Earth. Only Jupiter is bigger than Saturn.
questions.teachingFactText: Only Jupiter is bigger than Saturn.

questions.questionText: What are Saturn's rings made of?
questions.questionVoiceText: What are Saturn's rings made of?
questions.correctVoiceText: Brilliant! Saturn's rings spread a long way out from the planet. Saturn's rings are billions of little chunks of ice and rock.
questions.teachingFactText: Saturn's rings are billions of little chunks of ice and rock.

questions.questionText: Which is Saturn's biggest moon?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which is Saturn's biggest moon?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's it! Every other moon of Saturn is much smaller than Titan. Saturn's biggest moon is called Titan.
questions.teachingFactText: Saturn's biggest moon is called Titan.

questions.questionText: What is Saturn the giant ball made of?
questions.questionVoiceText: What is Saturn the giant ball made of?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's right! Hydrogen is the lightest gas there is. Saturn is a giant ball made of hydrogen and helium.
questions.teachingFactText: Saturn is a giant ball made of hydrogen and helium.

questions.questionText: Which of Saturn's moons has its own thick air all round it?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which of Saturn's moons has its own thick air all round it?
questions.correctVoiceText: You got it! A world with a thick layer of air around it has an atmosphere. Titan is the only moon with a thick atmosphere of its own.
questions.teachingFactText: Titan is the only moon with a thick atmosphere of its own.

questions.questionText: How many planets travel around our Sun?
questions.questionVoiceText: How many planets travel around our Sun?
questions.correctVoiceText: You got it! Eight planets travel around our Sun. Our solar system has eight planets, and Pluto is a dwarf planet, not one of the eight.
questions.teachingFactText: Our solar system has eight planets, and Pluto is a dwarf planet, not one of the eight.

questions.questionText: Which planet do we live on?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet do we live on?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's right! The answer is the planet you are standing on. Earth is our home planet.
questions.teachingFactText: Earth is our home planet.

questions.questionText: Counting out from the Sun, how many planets have solid, rocky ground?
questions.questionVoiceText: Counting out from the Sun, how many planets have solid, rocky ground?
questions.correctVoiceText: You got it! A rover needs solid ground under its wheels. The first four planets from the Sun have solid, rocky ground.
questions.teachingFactText: The first four planets from the Sun have solid, rocky ground.

questions.questionText: Which two planets are the gas giants?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which two planets are the gas giants?
questions.correctVoiceText: Yes! Neither of the gas giants has solid ground to stand on. Jupiter and Saturn are the two gas giants.
questions.teachingFactText: Jupiter and Saturn are the two gas giants.

questions.questionText: What shape is the Milky Way, the galaxy our solar system lives in?
questions.questionVoiceText: What shape is the Milky Way, the galaxy our solar system lives in?
questions.correctVoiceText: Spot on! A galaxy is a huge collection of stars, gas and dust, all held together by gravity. The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy.
questions.teachingFactText: The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy.

questions.questionText: Whereabouts in the Milky Way does our own Sun sit?
questions.questionVoiceText: Whereabouts in the Milky Way does our own Sun sit?
questions.correctVoiceText: Well done! The Sun is not in the middle of the galaxy. Our Sun sits in a small arm of the Milky Way called the Orion Arm.
questions.teachingFactText: Our Sun sits in a small arm of the Milky Way called the Orion Arm.

questions.questionText: Which two planets are called the ice giants?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which two planets are called the ice giants?
questions.correctVoiceText: Brilliant! The ice giants are the last two planets out from the Sun. Uranus and Neptune are the two ice giants.
questions.teachingFactText: Uranus and Neptune are the two ice giants.

questions.questionText: How long does our Sun take to travel once around the Milky Way?
questions.questionVoiceText: How long does our Sun take to travel once around the Milky Way?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's it! A full lap of the Milky Way takes far, far longer than our own lives. The Sun needs about 230 million years to go once around the Milky Way.
questions.teachingFactText: The Sun needs about 230 million years to go once around the Milky Way.

questions.questionText: Which star do all the planets travel around?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which star do all the planets travel around?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's right! The planets all travel around the Sun. The Sun is the only star in our solar system.
questions.teachingFactText: The Sun is the only star in our solar system.

questions.questionText: The Sun is about how many times wider than Earth?
questions.questionVoiceText: The Sun is about how many times wider than Earth?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's right! The Sun is far, far bigger than any planet. You could fit about 100 Earth-widths across the Sun.
questions.teachingFactText: You could fit about 100 Earth-widths across the Sun.

questions.questionText: What does the Sun's energy do for life on Earth?
questions.questionVoiceText: What does the Sun's energy do for life on Earth?
questions.correctVoiceText: You got it! Plants use sunlight to make their food. Sunlight and warmth from the Sun help almost all life on Earth.
questions.teachingFactText: Sunlight and warmth from the Sun help almost all life on Earth.

questions.questionText: What is the Sun made of?
questions.questionVoiceText: What is the Sun made of?
questions.correctVoiceText: Yes! The Sun's gas is so hot that it glows all by itself. The Sun is a ball of super-hot, charged gas called plasma.
questions.teachingFactText: The Sun is a ball of super-hot, charged gas called plasma.

questions.questionText: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth from the Sun?
questions.questionVoiceText: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth from the Sun?
questions.correctVoiceText: Spot on! Light is the fastest thing there is. Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach us from the Sun.
questions.teachingFactText: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach us from the Sun.

questions.questionText: Could you stand on the Sun if you had a spaceship?
questions.questionVoiceText: Could you stand on the Sun if you had a spaceship?
questions.correctAnswer: No — it is a ball of gas
choices: No — it is a ball of gas
Yes — it has a rocky surface
Yes — it has a sea of water
Yes — it is covered in clouds
questions.correctVoiceText: Well done! The Sun is far too hot to touch. The Sun has no solid ground to stand on.
questions.teachingFactText: The Sun has no solid ground to stand on.

questions.questionText: Which planet spins on its side, like a rolling ball?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet spins on its side, like a rolling ball?
questions.correctVoiceText: You got it! Uranus is the planet that spins on its side. Uranus is tilted so steeply that it appears to spin sideways as it rolls around the Sun.
questions.teachingFactText: Uranus is tilted so steeply that it appears to spin sideways as it rolls around the Sun.

questions.questionText: Which planet is the farthest from the Sun?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet is the farthest from the Sun?
questions.correctVoiceText: Yes! Neptune is the planet farthest from the Sun. Neptune is the eighth and most distant planet from the Sun.
questions.teachingFactText: Neptune is the eighth and most distant planet from the Sun.

questions.questionText: Uranus is a soft blue-green colour. What helps give it that colour?
questions.questionVoiceText: Uranus is a soft blue-green colour. What helps give it that colour?
questions.correctVoiceText: Yes! A planet's colour can come from the gas floating in its air. Methane in Uranus's air helps paint the planet blue-green.
questions.teachingFactText: Methane in Uranus's air helps paint the planet blue-green.

questions.questionText: Which planet was named after the Roman god of the sea?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which planet was named after the Roman god of the sea?
questions.correctVoiceText: Spot on! Neptune's moons are named after sea gods and nymphs in Greek stories. Neptune was named after the Roman god of the sea.
questions.teachingFactText: Neptune was named after the Roman god of the sea.

questions.questionText: How long does Neptune take to travel once around the Sun?
questions.questionVoiceText: How long does Neptune take to travel once around the Sun?
questions.correctVoiceText: Well done! The farther a planet is from the Sun, the longer its year takes. Neptune needs about 165 Earth years to go once around the Sun.
questions.teachingFactText: Neptune needs about 165 Earth years to go once around the Sun.

questions.questionText: How fast do the winds blow on Neptune?
questions.questionVoiceText: How fast do the winds blow on Neptune?
questions.correctAnswer: Faster than a thousand miles an hour
choices: Faster than a thousand miles an hour
Faster than four hundred miles an hour
Faster than forty miles an hour
questions.correctVoiceText: Brilliant! Neptune has the fastest winds of any planet. Neptune's winds blow faster than a thousand miles an hour.
questions.teachingFactText: Neptune's winds blow faster than a thousand miles an hour.

questions.questionText: Most asteroids travel around the Sun between which two planets?
questions.questionVoiceText: Most asteroids travel around the Sun between which two planets?
questions.correctVoiceText: Well done! Asteroids gather between Mars and Jupiter. Most asteroids orbit our Sun in the main belt between Mars and Jupiter.
questions.teachingFactText: Most asteroids orbit our Sun in the main belt between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.questionText: What is the largest object in the asteroid belt?
questions.questionVoiceText: What is the largest object in the asteroid belt?
questions.correctVoiceText: Brilliant! The answer is Ceres. Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt, and it is a dwarf planet too.
questions.teachingFactText: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt, and it is a dwarf planet too.

questions.questionText: Pluto is far beyond Neptune. What is Pluto called today?
questions.questionVoiceText: Pluto is far beyond Neptune. What is Pluto called today?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's it! Some older books counted Pluto as a planet. Pluto is a dwarf planet, far out beyond Neptune.
questions.teachingFactText: Pluto is a dwarf planet, far out beyond Neptune.

questions.questionText: Pluto's biggest moon is about half Pluto's size. What is that moon called?
questions.questionVoiceText: Pluto's biggest moon is about half Pluto's size. What is that moon called?
questions.correctVoiceText: That's right! Pluto and Charon circle around each other, like dance partners. Pluto's biggest moon, Charon, is about half as wide as Pluto.
questions.teachingFactText: Pluto's biggest moon, Charon, is about half as wide as Pluto.

questions.questionText: Which dwarf planet is the only one inside the main asteroid belt?
questions.questionVoiceText: Which dwarf planet is the only one inside the main asteroid belt?
questions.correctVoiceText: You got it! The inner solar system means the part closest to the Sun. Ceres is the inner solar system's one and only dwarf planet.
questions.teachingFactText: Ceres is the inner solar system's one and only dwarf planet.

questions.questionText: Added together, are all the asteroids in the belt heavier than the Moon?
questions.questionVoiceText: Added together, are all the asteroids in the belt heavier than the Moon?
questions.correctAnswer: No — together they weigh less than the Moon
choices: No — together they weigh less than the Moon
Yes — much heavier than the Moon
Yes — about the same as the Moon
No — they weigh nothing at all
questions.correctVoiceText: Yes! Every asteroid in the belt is smaller than the Moon. Added together, all the asteroids weigh less than the Moon.
questions.teachingFactText: Added together, all the asteroids weigh less than the Moon.
